name: YAGEO-cc-x5r
title: X5R multilayer ceramic chip capacitors, general purpose and high capacitance, 0201 to 1210, 4 V to 50 V
summary: The CC X5R series are class 2 surface-mount multilayer ceramic capacitors in six case sizes, 0201 to 1210, spanning 100 pF to 220 µF at rated voltages of 4 V, 6.3 V, 10 V, 16 V, 25 V and 50 V, with ±10% or ±20% tolerance. Capacitance holds within ±15% from –55 °C to +85 °C. Terminations are nickel-barrier, tin-plated and lead-free; the parts are RoHS and halogen-free compliant, MSL 1, and delivered taped on reels or in bulk cases. Each size, voltage and value carries a thickness code, and the range splits into a general-purpose and a high-capacitance group with different test limits.

operation.text: Interleaved metal electrode layers are stacked inside a ceramic dielectric body; every other layer reaches one end of the chip and the rest reach the other. Each end carries a lead-free termination of tin plated over a nickel barrier (NiSn).

L1 is body length, W width and T thickness. L2 and L3 are the lengths of the two terminations along the body, and L4 is the gap between them. The dimension code in the part's capacitance-range cell sets which tolerance band of L1, W and T applies.
Uses named for the series: PCs, hard disk drives, game PCs, power supplies, DVD players, mobile phones and data processing.

operation.topic: General purpose and high capacitance groups
operation.text: Within each size and voltage the lower values belong to the general-purpose group and the higher values to the high-capacitance group. The high-capacitance group is held to wider limits after damp heat and endurance (±20% capacitance change, D.F. up to twice initial) and is endurance-tested at 1.0 or 1.5 times rated voltage instead of 2.0 times.

0201 and 1210 parts are for reflow only. In 0402, 0603, 0805 and 1206, the lower values up to 100 nF, 1 µF, 2.2 µF and 2.2 µF can go through reflow or wave; higher values in those sizes are reflow only.

Every measurement is taken once the whole capacitor has settled at the measuring temperature; a test's own recovery period is normally long enough for that. Class 2 capacitance and D.F. are measured at 20 °C, 24 hours after annealing.
